newsitem.title: USA: Iowa soybean harvest making rapid progress.
newsitem.headline: Iowa soybean harvest making rapid progress.

text.p: Soybean harvesting in Iowa made rapid progress in the week to Sunday but corn harvesting advanced more slowly, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
The report noted some corn producers were waiting for corn to dry down before rolling the combines.
"Last week's dry winds provided perfect pre-harvest conditions," the report said.
Iowa's soybeans were 59 percent harvested as of Sunday, up from 22 percent a week earlier and 56 percent at the same time last year. The five-year average stood at 63 percent.
Ninety-six percent of soybeans were dropping leaves, versus last year's 99 percent and the normal 98 percent.

Corn harvesting stood at just eight percent done, only marginally up from the previous week's five percent. It remained well behind last year's 26 percent and the five-year average, which also stood at 26 percent.
Ninety four percent of corn was mature, down from last year's 99 percent and the average pace of 96 percent.
Topsoil moisture rated one percent surplus, 67 percent adequate, 28 percent short and four percent very short.
